From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-08-09T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Lumina connector — MSA/DPA + SOW attached (redlines)

Forwarding Lumina docs with initial comments. High-level summary of our asks (non-exhaustive):

1) Indemnity & liability: propose mutual indemnity; liability cap at 3x fees (for the first year of contract or minimum $250k), explicit carve-out for IP infringement.
2) Termination: 60 days for convenience; 30 days for cure on material breaches.
3) Data processing scope: limit processing to inference inputs, model outputs, and minimal routing metadata. No broad "customer data" catch-alls.
4) Data deletion & retention: require deletion of inference data within 30 days of termination except for aggregated telemetry; define retention exceptions for billing/abuse.
5) Audit rights: allow review of SOC2 Type II report and one evidence review per 12 months; restrict intrusive onsite audits for hosted offerings. Request Lumina provide SOC2 report and subprocessor list via secure link.
6) Subprocessors: require notice within 30 days of onboarding new subprocessors and reasonable right to object for high-risk subprocessors.
7) Encryption / KMS: for hosted customers we require encryption at rest + in transit; KMS integration required only for Private deployments. For enterprise-only deals, support for a customer-managed KMS is required.
8) SLOs & credits: specify a baseline latency SLA for the connector if they commit to production support; otherwise pilot is best-effort with onboarding targets.

Monica: please confirm that the SOW milestones match expected engineering ramp (3x integration sprints + security review).

Ive put line edits into the attached redline PDF. If Lumina can confirm SOC2 + subprocessors we can narrow the DPA concerns quickly.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the thorough review and the redlines. A few points from our side: 

- Indemnity cap: we can accept a reciprocal approach but our standard cap is 2x fees. Can you confirm whether 2x would be acceptable or provide rationale for 3x so we can escalate internally?
- Termination: 60 days looks fine.
- Audit: we can provide SOC2 Type II and a subprocessor list (attached as lumina-subprocessors-20270809.csv). For hosted customers we prefer the documentation-only audit approach; we can negotiate limited evidence gathering in a secure environment.
- KMS: our hosted offering does not expose customer KMS keys. We can offer an enterprise private deployment with KMS integration if Lumina requires customer-managed keys; alternately, we can add encryption-at-rest assurances plus key separation controls.

Ive attached the subprocessor list and a short note from our security team. If that satisfies the audit/Subprocessor asks, we can move to finalize the DPA language around retention and deletion.

Attachments: lumina-subprocessors-20270809.csv, lumina-security-note.pdf
